subject: Ranching and settlement baseline
observation: The exact pre-town ranching chronology and townsite creation remain unverified. Town-company records and 1892-1903 assessments are cataloged.
limit: Do not turn broad catalog collection dates into dates for the town-company volume.

subject: Railway corridor forms
observation: The contemporary 1902 railway report describes the connection at Santa Rosa. Cuervo's exact station-opening and plat dates are still missing.
limit: Regional railway context, not a Cuervo opening certificate.

subject: Early mercantile activity
observation: A later historical report places Bond expansion to Cuervo in the early 1900s; the archive catalogs a Bond & Wiest ledger for 1904-1908.
limit: The ledger has not been read; no opening date, revenue or customer geography established.

subject: Santa Rosa already has regional functions
observation: Sanborn maps identify government, banking, wholesale premises and other services before Route 66.
limit: Comparison-town baseline; no inference that its customers all came from Cuervo.

subject: Clipper origins
observation: The LOC catalog says January 1909; the April 15, 1921 paper says it is entering its fourteenth year. Surviving local scans begin January 1910.
limit: Founding accounts are inconsistent; the first surviving issue is not the first published issue.

subject: Telephone connection
observation: The Clipper reports completion of the Cuervo-Montoya telephone line.
limit: Dated report of improved communication; no subscriber count.

subject: Passing cattle handled at Cuervo
observation: Five carloads of cattle were unloaded the previous Sunday to feed and rest while en route to Kansas City; several reportedly died.
limit: Direct report of livestock handling, not evidence the cattle originated near Cuervo.

subject: Commercial and medical services
observation: Advertisements name Bond & Wiest, Big Jo Lumber, Cuervo Drug Store, Rock Island Boarding House, two physicians and a visiting dentist.
limit: Advertisements establish offers at this date, not occupancy, receipts or full-time staffing.

subject: Livery exit and planned garage conversion
observation: T. L. Lewis reportedly closed out his livery business and entered cattle dealing; Long Commission Company announced it would take over the livery barn and convert it to a garage.
limit: Owner exit and proposed reuse. Completion of the conversion is not established here.

subject: Sheep shipped and merchants traded
observation: The paper reports fourteen cars of sheep loaded at Cuervo for Kansas, a separate purchase of over 4,000 sheep from Bond & Wiest, and produce unloaded for the merchant.
limit: Do not equate the fourteen cars with the separate 4,000-head purchase; the report does not explicitly link them.

subject: Townsite promotion
observation: A list of purchasers of lots in the Thompson Townsite addition appears in the paper.
limit: A contemporary sales claim; deeds, occupancy and the original town plat remain unverified.

subject: School bonds approved
observation: The Sixth (Cuervo) School District reportedly approved $4,000 in bonds with one opposing vote for a new stone school building.
limit: Vote authorizes investment; it is not a completion date.

subject: School draws families
observation: Prof. Haight reports 67 enrolled pupils; the paper says families are moving into Cuervo from the surrounding country for schooling.
limit: Enrollment is reported, and the migration statement is qualitative. The forecast of 100 pupils is not an observed count.

subject: Early population observations
observation: Cuervo precinct totals are 545 and 438, respectively.
limit: The 1920 compendium warns of redistricting. These are not fixed-footprint town counts.

subject: School financing advances
observation: The paper says bonds have been sold and the board is ready for bids on a stone school with four rooms.
limit: Stronger evidence of implementation than the earlier vote, but still not completion.

subject: School under construction
observation: Contractor J. B. Colvin is identified as in charge of erecting the new school.
limit: Construction is underway by this report.

subject: Lumber stock being withdrawn
observation: Big Jo Lumber is reported to be shipping out its stock and cutting prices on what remains.
limit: Evidence of stock withdrawal/liquidation activity; the final yard closure and reason are unverified.

subject: Depot platform improved
observation: Section foreman Hanson reportedly widened and improved the depot platform.
limit: Railway facilities were receiving work alongside other commercial changes.

subject: New school in use
observation: The paper describes a new two-story school, two employed teachers and an expectation of needing a third; it again reports seasonal moves into Cuervo for school.
limit: The third teacher is a forecast. Exact opening day and identity of today's surviving building require confirmation.

subject: Hanson-Cuervo mail route discontinued
observation: The Post Office report records discontinuance of the 7.5-mile, three-round-trip-weekly route because Hanson lacked a suitable postmaster candidate.
limit: Loss of a feeder route; Cuervo's own post office did not close at this date.

subject: Oklahoma Hotel changes hands
observation: S. P. Morison is reported to have purchased the Oklahoma Hotel from Mrs. Lizzie Mason the preceding Monday.
limit: A sale, not a closure. The buyer is listed as Morrison in later directories.

subject: Medical and automobile services
observation: Dr. A. A. Sanford advertises at the Cuervo drugstore; S. P. Morison advertises the Ford Garage, repairs and gasoline.
limit: Dated service offers before Route 66 designation.

subject: Broad business directory baseline
observation: The Cuervo entry lists two hotels, Golden Rule Garage, several merchants, a school principal, postmaster, railway/express/telegraph agent and stage/mail line to Lucille.
limit: A directory snapshot; neighborhood population 350 is not the census precinct count.

subject: Pooled support for a doctor
observation: W. B. Terry of Newkirk proposes $1 per family per month to attract a physician for the locality, believing 100 families would agree.
limit: Proposal and perceived access problem. No 100 actual subscribers or successful recruitment established.

subject: Santa Rosa competes for trade
observation: Moise Bros. advertises that savings justify a trip even over a long distance; Santa Rosa Mercantile explicitly prints its Santa Rosa address.
limit: Evidence of solicitation across distance, not measured diversion of Cuervo spending.

subject: Garage reopens
observation: The Cuervo garage reportedly reopens after several months closed, with Harrison Bros. as mechanics.
limit: Direct evidence that at least one closure was temporary.

subject: Physician called from Duran
observation: Dr. A. A. Sanford of Duran is reported called to see a Cuervo child.
limit: Matches the name advertised at Cuervo in 1918; suggests a changed practice base, not the disappearance of every local doctor.

subject: Garage and blacksmith service advertised
observation: M. D. Harrison advertises gasoline, oils, accessories, engine work and blacksmithing at the old Ozark Trail Garage building.
limit: A named business and location clue; identity with the earlier Golden Rule or 1910 barn is unproved.

subject: Merchants and hotels persist
observation: The directory still lists Armijo, Bond & Wiest, two hotels and other enterprises. It changes the Rock Island proprietor to J. L. Foster and the school principal to Alma E. Squire.
limit: Proprietor and personnel turnover; omissions alone cannot date closures.

subject: Delayed train boosts trade
observation: A westbound limited was held at Cuervo all Wednesday by a freight wreck toward Santa Rosa; the paper reports a busy day for local hotels and stores.
limit: Dated connection between a transport interruption and local commerce; no receipts or normal baseline.

subject: Clipper financial withdrawal
observation: Katharine A. Hicks announces withdrawal from financial involvement, reports losses, and advocates concentration of newspaper support at the county seat.
limit: Political purpose and her associate's Santa Rosa paper also matter. This does not establish exact cessation.

subject: Possible newspaper cessation
observation: The LOC catalog notes possible cessation in 1923, citing Pearce S. Grove's New Mexico newspapers.
limit: The question mark is material. No final issue or definitive closure notice obtained.

subject: Route 66 era begins
observation: Route 66 designation enters the chronology after the businesses, institutions and pressures documented above.
limit: Designation is not the beginning of road travel or all tourist trade.

subject: Passenger access is directional
observation: The timetable offers a morning trip from Cuervo to Tucumcari and an evening return; the Santa Rosa pairing requires an overnight stay.
limit: A travel opportunity, not evidence that particular people shopped in either place.

subject: Santa Rosa commercial concentration
observation: Santa Rosa reports 44.5% of county retail sales with 16.0% of county population; Cuervo precinct counts 287 residents in 1930.
limit: Business and population refer to different reference years; Cuervo receipts are not separately known.

subject: Southwest road realignment
observation: The NRHP narrative identifies FAP 114-C and plans dated December 1, 1932.
limit: Historical highway documentation; parcel-level Cuervo effects remain open.

subject: Paving east of Cuervo
observation: The Montoya-Cuervo nomination dates hard surfacing to 1936, citing 1935 plans.
limit: Not a demonstrated date of economic collapse.

subject: Pre-interstate demographic contraction
observation: Cuervo precinct has 188 residents, down from 287 in 1930.
limit: A 34.5% decline in the reported precinct; no exact within-decade turning point.

subject: County livestock sales expand
observation: Guadalupe County cattle/calves sold rise from 7,399 in 1939 to 19,724 in 1944, then 17,595 in 1949.
limit: County cattle flows, not Cuervo shipments, profits or jobs.

subject: Cuervo feed dealer remains listed
observation: An El Rancho Milling advertisement names Bond & Wiest of Cuervo among its dealers. The adjacent article describes the Clovis mill, rail spur and direct truck deliveries to ranches.
limit: Evidence of a dealer relationship; neither sales volume nor bypassing of a particular Cuervo merchant is measured.

subject: Working community and small rebound
observation: Cuervo precinct counts 210 people, 22 more than 1940. Main occupation descriptions include ranching, railway work, retail, teaching, postal and food/service work.
limit: Residents' occupations do not locate every employer inside the settlement.

subject: Real cattle-price downturn
observation: Statewide real beef-cattle prices fall 51.7% from the 1951 peak to 1956 in the project series.
limit: Potential economic pressure; local business losses have not been attributed to it.

subject: Southwest highway relocated
observation: The old alignment is superseded before the interstate project.
limit: Separate change in access; affected premises and business losses remain to be linked.

subject: Train-order-office designation disappears
observation: The designation is present in September 1956 and absent in the October 1958 operating timetable.
limit: Does not date the last employee or freight agency closure.

subject: Advertised passenger stops disappear
observation: Stops are still advertised April 27; the October 26 operating timetable has no regular, flag or conditional stop marker at Cuervo.
limit: Bracket for scheduled passenger service; not the end of railway use or all cattle loading.

subject: School closure lead
observation: A later published account dates school closure to 1958. Administrative records have not confirmed the date or reason.
limit: Keep this as a lead, not a verified endpoint for the school.

subject: Documented interstate construction
observation: NTSB describes project I-040-5(18)1283 near Cuervo, approximately mileposts 282.7-290.7.
limit: Exact coverage of Exit 291, property takings and local access changes still require project files.

subject: Siding remains listed
observation: A railway timetable still lists the Cuervo siding.
limit: Physical/operating listing is not proof of livestock-loading use.

subject: Through Golden State service ends
observation: The through passenger train is discontinued after Cuervo's scheduled local stops had disappeared.
limit: Two distinct passenger-service events.

subject: Santa Rosa interstate bypass
observation: An official state memorial dates Santa Rosa's I-40 completion to 1972.
limit: Its 1960-1970 growth precedes this event; the two towns' exposure is not identical by assumption.

subject: Freight administration persists without local agent
observation: Rock Island lists Cuervo with no agent, separate location/accounting codes and billing assigned to Tucumcari.
limit: Administrative identity persists; actual carloads, livestock acceptance and local payroll remain unverified.

subject: Post office formally discontinued
observation: USPS records Cuervo's discontinuance and reassignment as a place name under Newkirk while retaining ZIP 88417.
limit: Administrative effective date, not necessarily the last date a staffed counter operated.

subject: Funeral Mass announced
observation: Dorothy Chavez's funeral notice announces Mass at Santo Nino, Cuervo, and names her restoration involvement.
limit: An announced service and stewardship evidence; not a regular-service schedule.

subject: Catholic mission affiliation
observation: The archdiocesan directory lists Santo Nino, Cuervo, as a mission of St. Rose of Lima, Santa Rosa.
limit: Administrative affiliation, not attendance or frequency of priest visits.

subject: Named ranch base outside Cuervo
observation: Jim Armendariz says his father purchased the ranch outside Cuervo in 2020 and the operation works from there.
limit: A retrospective first-person account; other leases extend beyond Cuervo.

subject: Parish financial activity
observation: A St. Rose bulletin records a Cuervo Function receipt of $170.
limit: Does not identify event location, attendance or regular Mass frequency.

subject: Ranching continues
observation: A conservation-award announcement and ranch-family interview independently identify a current Cuervo-area operation.
limit: Contemporary ranching is established; historical continuity on every parcel and local spending shares are not.
